facts.fact_text: At the material time the first applicant was a member of the youth committee of an opposition party called the Popular Front Party of Azerbaijan (Azərbaycan Xalq Cəbhəsi Partiyası – the PFPA).
At the material time the second applicant was a chairman of a youth organisation called Azad Genclik.
Both applicants participated in a number of unauthorised peaceful demonstrations organised by the opposition.
The second applicant attended the demonstration of 11 March 2011.
The second applicant attended the demonstration of 20 October 2012.
The first applicant attended the demonstration of 20 October 2012.
The first applicant attended the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
According to the first applicant, he also intended to participate in the demonstration of 11 March 2011.
According to the first applicant, he was actively promoting public participation in the assembly of 11 March 2011 on online social networks.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful and were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The participants in the demonstrations were demanding democratic reforms in Azerbaijan.
The participants in the demonstrations were demanding free and fair elections.
The participants in the demonstrations were protesting against impediments on freedom of assembly.
The demonstration of 11 March 2011 was attended by the second applicant.
The demonstration of 20 October 2012 was attended by both the first applicant and the second applicant.
The demonstration of 17 November 2012 was attended by the first applicant.
In the course of many of those unauthorised peaceful demonstrations, both applicants were arrested and convicted.
The Nasimi District Court convicted the first applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences and sentenced him to ten days' administrative detention.

The Sabail District Court convicted the applicants under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer) in each case related to the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012.

In the proceedings related to his participation in the demonstration of 20 October 2012, the second applicant was also convicted by the Sabail District Court under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (violation of rules on holding public assemblies).
The applicants were sentenced to various periods of administrative detention as set out in the Appendix.

The administrative-offence report stated that the first applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).

In each case following the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012, the applicants were charged with an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).

The Sabail District Court convicted the applicants under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer) in each case related to the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012.

In the proceedings related to his participation in the demonstration of 20 October 2012, the second applicant was also convicted by the Sabail District Court under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (violation of rules on holding public assemblies).

After the amendments introduced by Law no. 135-IVQD of 31 May 2011, which entered into force on 1 July 2011, Article 410.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that a copy of the administrative offence report shall be given to an individual who is subject to the administrative offence proceedings or to a representative of a legal entity.

After the amendments introduced by Law no. 135-IVQD of 31 May 2011, which entered into force on 1 July 2011, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that an aggrieved person in administrative offence proceedings has the right to a copy of the administrative offence report.

A summary of the relevant provisions concerning administrative proceedings in Azerbaijan is contained in the judgment in Huseynli and Others v. Azerbaijan (nos. 67360/11, 67964/11 and 69379/11, §§ 67-77, 11 February 2016).

A summary of the relevant provisions concerning freedom of assembly and the organisation and holding of public assemblies in Azerbaijan is contained in the judgment in Huseynli and Others v. Azerbaijan (nos. 67360/11, 67964/11 and 69379/11, §§ 67-77, 11 February 2016).

A summary of the relevant provisions concerning administrative proceedings in Azerbaijan is also contained in the judgment in Ibrahimov and Others v. Azerbaijan (nos. 69234/11, 69252/11 and 69335/11, §§ 44-59, 11 February 2016).

A summary of the relevant provisions concerning freedom of assembly and the organisation and holding of public assemblies in Azerbaijan is also contained in the judgment in Ibrahimov and Others v. Azerbaijan (nos. 69234/11, 69252/11 and 69335/11, §§ 44-59, 11 February 2016).

In each case following the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012, the applicants were charged with an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).

The Sabail District Court convicted the applicants under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer) in each case related to the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012.

In the proceedings related to his participation in the demonstration of 20 October 2012, the second applicant was also convicted by the Sabail District Court under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (violation of rules on holding public assemblies).
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 20 October 2012 at the site indicated by the organisers.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted in general terms that the assembly of 17 November 2012 would not be in accordance with the Law on Freedom of Assembly.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted that the assembly of 17 November 2012 itself would be impractical.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful and were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The participants in the demonstrations were demanding democratic reforms in Azerbaijan.
The participants in the demonstrations were demanding free and fair elections.
The participants in the demonstrations were protesting against impediments on freedom of assembly.
All three demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012 were dispersed as soon as the protesters began to gather.
Both applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations of the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012.
According to the applicants, they were never served with a copy of the administrative-offence reports or with other documents from their case files following their arrests during the demonstrations.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after their arrests during the demonstrations or while they were in police custody.
According to the applicants, the respective hearings before the Sabail District Court were very brief.

According to the applicants, members of the public were not allowed inside the courtroom during the hearings before the Sabail District Court, even though the court had not taken a formal decision to close the hearings to the public.
According to the applicants, they were not given an opportunity to appoint lawyers of their own choosing at the hearings before the Sabail District Court.
During the Sabail District Court hearing of 20 October 2012, the court did not question any witnesses.
During the Sabail District Court hearing of 17 November 2012, the court did not question any witnesses.
According to the first applicant, he was never served with a copy of the administrative-offence report or with other documents from his case file following his arrest on 4 March 2011.
According to the first applicant, he was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest on 4 March 2011 or while he was in police custody.
According to the first applicant, he was not given an opportunity to appoint a lawyer of his own choosing at the hearing before the Nasimi District Court on 4 March 2011.
According to the transcript of the Nasimi District Court's hearing on 4 March 2011, the State-funded lawyer Mr O.A. did not make any oral or written submissions on behalf of the first applicant.

The Baku Court of Appeal did not address the first applicant's request to have his mobile-phone call records examined in respect of the date and time of the alleged administrative offence on 4 March 2011.
According to the applicants, they were never served with a copy of the administrative-offence reports or with other documents from their case files following their arrests during the demonstrations.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after their arrests during the demonstrations or while they were in police custody.
According to the applicants, they were not given an opportunity to appoint lawyers of their own choosing at the hearings before the Sabail District Court.
